analysis.title: Treasury QRA: Who Pays for Duration
key_insights: Treasury cannot change how much it borrows at Wednesday's refunding, but it decides how much duration the market must own. In the August-October quarter, 20- and 30-year bonds were 11.6% of coupon dollars sold but 30.5% of the rate risk (DV01).
The shift toward bills is happening by default, not by design. Shorter issuance swaps duration risk for refinancing and policy-rate risk for Treasury, so it is not cheaper funding.
Goldman's base case is no change on Wednesday. The key signal is whether the guidance that coupon sizes hold for 'at least the next several quarters' survives.

Treasury has kept nominal coupon auction sizes unchanged for 10 refunding quarters. In August it said it expected to keep nominal coupon and FRN sizes unchanged for 'at least the next several quarters.'

The same borrowing amount creates very different duration. USD 1tn of 13-week bills equals about USD 31bn of 10-year-equivalent risk, USD 1tn of 10-year notes equals USD 1tn, and USD 1tn of 30-year bonds equals about USD 1.9tn.

The Fed has been buying bills since mid-December 2025. SOMA bill holdings rose from USD 195.5bn to USD 571.5bn by 28 Oct, and the Fed's share of bills outstanding went from 3.6% at end-2025 to 7.9% at end-September. The support is fading: USD 56bn of bills added in February versus USD 11bn through 28 Oct.

Treasury bought back USD 16bn of 10-30 year paper over eight operations in May-July. The August-October schedule allowed at least USD 34bn over nine operations, against USD 111bn of 20s and 30s issued in the quarter. Funding buybacks with bills lowers market duration, while funding them with long coupons largely offsets the effect.
2y yields rose 111bp year to date versus 48bp for the 30y. The NY Fed ACM 10y term premium rose to 0.99% on 7 Oct and fell back to 0.66% on 29 Oct, which eases immediate pressure on the long end.

Bill-heavy financing ties Treasury's interest bill more tightly to the policy rate. If higher interest costs eventually constrain monetary policy, fiscal risk can reappear through inflation expectations and the expected policy path.
This is not Operation Twist. Coupon sizes are frozen rather than cut, and bills were 22.4% of marketable debt in September 2026 versus 21.9% in December 2024 and 21.5% in September 2025.
Treasury also competes for long-term capital with a capital-intensive corporate cycle.
Borrowing estimates for Oct-Dec and Jan-Mar are due later on 2 Nov. A large upside surprise would pressure the current coupon guidance.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Issuance is shifting toward bills by default as coupon sizes stay frozen.
Up from 21.9% in December 2024 and 21.5% in September 2025, a small and passive increase.
Up from 3.6% at end-2025 as the Fed bought bills, but the pace of purchases has slowed.
Down from 0.99% on 7 Oct, which reduces immediate pressure on the long end.
The front end has repriced faster than the 30y (+48bp), so bill-heavy funding sits in the part of the curve that moved most.

macro_indicators.indicator: Goldman base case for Nov refunding
macro_indicators.reading: Coupon sizes unchanged, guidance retained, long-end buybacks extended (65%)
macro_indicators.interpretation: The market should see no change in coupon sizes. The wording on 'at least the next several quarters' is the signal.

risk_factors: A softening of the 'at least the next several quarters' coupon guidance would open the door to coupon increases and add duration supply.
A large upside surprise in the borrowing estimates due 2 Nov.
Heavier bill funding raises Treasury's refinancing and policy-rate risk and ties interest costs to the policy rate.
Fading Fed bill purchases (USD 11bn through 28 Oct versus USD 56bn in February) leave more bill supply for private investors.
Competition from capital-intensive corporate borrowing for long-term capital.
vol_and_positioning: Long-end bearish scenario (20%): guidance softened, opening the door to future coupon increases.
Long-end bullish scenario (15%): larger or more frequent long-end buybacks, or clearer comfort with a higher bill share.
A large upside surprise in the Oct-Dec and Jan-Mar borrowing estimates would pressure current coupon guidance.

tension_points.bull_case: Shifting issuance toward bills means investors absorb less duration, and the long-end bullish scenario (15%) includes larger buybacks or clearer comfort with a higher bill share.
tension_points.bear_case: Shorter funding does not mean cheaper funding. It moves issuance to the part of the curve that has repriced fastest (2y +111bp YTD), and ties Treasury's interest bill to the policy rate, so fiscal risk can reappear through inflation expectations and the policy path.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The refunding statement dropping or softening the 'at least the next several quarters' coupon guidance, or a large upside surprise in the Oct-Dec and Jan-Mar borrowing estimates.

theme_stances.key_argument: Treasury sets the maturity mix, so the supply of duration matters, not just the supply of debt.
theme_stances.evidence: the supply of duration matters, not just the supply of debt
